definition: A concept defined as the opposing but complementary qualities of interrelated entities/ phenomena in the natural world.
Yin is the opposite of yang. The qualities of yin include cold/cool, dimness, descending, stillness, introversion, heaviness, etc.
Yang is the opposite of yin. The qualities of yang include warm/hot, bright, ascending, movement, extroversion, light, clearness, etc.
Yin qi is the opposite of yang qi. The qualities of yin qi include condensation, moistening, inhibition, etc.
Yang qi is the opposite of yin qi. The qualities of yang qi include warming, activating, excitation, etc.
Yin and yang mutually affect and interact with one another.
Yin and yang mutually oppose and restrain one another.
Yin and yang mutually support one another.
Yin and yang have reciprocal roots and cannot be separated.

term_en: Yin and yang wax and wane
definition: Dynamic waxing and waning between yin and yang.
Under certain circumstances, yin may transform into yang and yang into yin.
When yin develops to its extremity, it will transform into yang.
When yang develops to its extremity, it will transform into yin.
A harmonious state between yin and yang, when yin qi is in balance and yang qi is secured within the body.

term_en: Spontaneous harmonization between yin and yang
definition: The tendency for yin and yang to spontaneously and mutually harmonize.
Without yang, yin cannot come into being.
Without yin, yang cannot grow and develop.
When yin is further divided into yin and yang, the yin aspect of yin is called yin within yin.
When yin is further divided into yin and yang, the yang aspect of yin is called yang within yin.
When yang is further divided into yin and yang, the yang aspect of yang is called yang within yang.
When yang is further divided into yin and yang, the yin aspect of yang is called yin within yang.
When yang qi brings things to life, yin qi grows and enables endurance.
In regard to the changing seasons, it is the nature of yang to kill and break things down and the nature of yin to store.
A collective term for Jueyin, Shaoyin and Taiyin; Shaoyang, Yangming and Taiyang.
The interactions and changes among the five categories of phenomena represented by wood, fire, earth, metal and water.

term_en: Wood is characterized by bending and straightening
definition: The nature of wood is to bend and straighten as it grows. The wood element is used to express growth, bearing upwards, effusion, free flow, etc.

term_en: Fire is characterized by flaming upward
definition: The nature of fire is to flame upwards. The fire element is used to express warmth, rising, flourishing, etc.

term_en: Earth is characterized by sowing and reaping
definition: The soil of the earth is where crops are sown and reaped. The earth element is used to express transformation, carrying, embracing, etc.

term_en: Metal is characterized by yielding and changing
definition: The nature of metal is to be adaptable and changeable. The metal element is used to express chilliness, descending, purification, etc.

term_en: Water is characterized by moistening and descending
definition: The nature of water is to be moist and flow downwards. The water element is used to express coldness, moistening, downward movement, storing, etc.

synonyms_en: Mutual generation among the five elements
definition: The five elements mutually engender and support one another. The sequential engendering and supporting relationships among the five elements are, specifically, wood generates fire, fire generates earth, earth generates metal, metal generates water and water generates wood. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

synonyms_en: Mutual controlling among the five elements
definition: The five elements mutually control and restrain one another. The sequential restraining relationships among the five elements are, specifically, wood restrains earth, earth restrains water, water restrains fire, fire restrains metal, and metal restrains wood.

term_en: The five elements mutually control and transform
definition: A balanced, harmonized state maintained by mutual generating and restraining relationships among the five elements.

term_en: The five elements overcome and retaliate
definition: The five elements have the actions of overcoming and retaliating with one another.

term_en: The five elements mutually over-restrain one another
definition: Excessive restraint of an element over the element it controls.

term_en: The five elements mutually counter-restrain one another
synonyms_en: Reverse restraining/ insulting among the five elements
definition: A restraining element becomes controlled by the element it controls.
In the five elements, the qi of one element gives birth to the succeeding element.
In the five elements, the qi of one element is born from the previous element.
In the five elements, when an illness in the mother organ is passed to the child organ.

term_en: Child’ s illness affects the mother
synonyms_en: Child stealing the mother’ s qi
definition: In the five elements, when an illness in a child organ affects the mother organ.
The five directions are east, west, south, north and center. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, metal, fire, water and earth respectively.
A fifth seasonal period occurring between the seasons of summer and autumn. It can also refer to the period of the last eighteen days of each season.
The five seasons are spring, summer, late summer, autumn and winter. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The prevailing climate qualities of the five seasons are wind, summer heat, dampness, dryness and cold. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The five transformative states are birth, growth, transformation, harvest and storage. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The five colours are green, red, yellow, white and black. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The five flavours are sour, bitter, sweet, pungent and salty. In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The five musical notes are jué (mi), zhǐ(sol), gōng (do), shāng (re), and yǔ (la). In the five elements, they are associated with wood, fire, earth, metal and water respectively.
The word“zang”means the internal organs; and the word“xiang”means the outward manifestations of physiological functions and pathological changes of the internal organs.
A collective term for the internal organs of human beings, including five zang organs, six fu organs and extraordinary organs.
A collective term for the five internal organs—the heart, liver, spleen/pancreas, lung and kidney. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
A collective term for the six internal organs: gallbladder, stomach, large intestine, small intestine, urinary bladder, and sanjiao (literally translated into“triple energizer”).
A collective term for brain, marrow, bone, vessels, gallbladder and uterus. These organs are extraordinary because they store like zang organs.

The zang–fu organs mutually correspond with one another, with a (yin) interior–(yang) exterior connection between the zang and fu organs. Specifically, the heart is internally–externally connected with the small intestine, the lung with the large intestine, the spleen with the stomach, the liver with the gallbladder, the kidney with the urinary bladder, and the pericardium with sanjiao.

term_en: Storage of the five zang organs
definition: The heart stores the spirit; the lung stores the corporeal soul; the liver stores the ethereal soul; the spleen stores the intent; and the kidney stores the will.

term_en: Governance of the five zang organs
definition: The heart governs blood vessels; the lung governs the skin; the spleen governs the flesh; the liver governs the sinew/tendon; and the kidney governs the bones.

term_en: Fluids of the five zang organs
definition: The fluid of the heart is sweat; the fluid of the lung is nasal mucus; the fluid of the spleen is thin saliva; the fluid of the liver is tears; and the fluid of the kidney is the thick saliva.

term_en: Lustres of the five zang organs
definition: The lustre of the heart shows in the face; the lustre of the lung shows in the skin hair; the lustre of the spleen shows in the lips; the lustre of the liver shows in the nails; and the lustre of the kidney shows in the hair.

term_en: Opening of the five zang organs
definition: The heart opens into the tongue; the lung opens into the nose; the spleen opens into the mouth; the liver opens into the eyes; and the kidney opens into the ears.

term_en: Emotions of the five zang organs
definition: The emotion of the heart is joy; the emotion of the lung is grief; the emotion of the spleen is overthinking; the emotion of the liver is anger; and the emotion of the kidney is fear.

term_en: Dislikes of the five zang organs
definition: The heart dislikes heat; the lung dislikes cold; the spleen dislikes dampness; the liver dislikes wind; and the kidney dislikes dryness.
The qi stored by the heart, as opposed to heart blood. It is the driving force of physiological activities of the heart.
The blood stored by the heart, as opposed to heart qi. It is the material foundation of physiological activities of the heart.
The yin essence of the heart, as opposed to heart yang. It refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the heart’s function.
The yang qi of the heart, as opposed to heart yin. It refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspect of the heart’s function.
A functional system composed of the heart, small intestine, blood vessels, face, tongue and heart meridian.
It refers to the heart, the foundation of human life.
It refers to the heart. The heart is called the organ of monarch because it stores the spirit (i.e. the foundation of life).

term_en: The heart governs the bright spirit
synonyms_en: The heart governs spirit and/or mind The heart governs mental activities
definition: The heart dominates the vital activities and governs mental, conscious and thinking activities.

term_en: The heart governs the blood and vessels
definition: The normal functioning of the heart in pumping blood to circulate within the vessels.

term_en: The lustre of the heart shows in the face
synonyms_en: The lustre of the heart shows in complexion
definition: The colour and lustre of the face manifest the functioning of the heart. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: The heart opens into the tongue
definition: The tongue is nourished by heart qi and blood. It is the opening orifice of the heart.

term_en: The tongue is the expression of the heart
definition: The physiological functions and pathological changes of heart can manifest on the tongue.

term_en: The fluid of the heart is sweat
definition: Sweat is associated with the heart.

term_en: The vessels are the tissue of the heart
definition: The blood vessels are associated with the heart.

term_en: The emotion of the heart is joy
definition: Joy is associated with the heart.
The heart is intolerant of heat. It is fire in nature and can be easily damaged by fire heat.

term_en: The pairing between the heart and small intestine
definition: The heart is externally–internally paired with the small intestine through meridians.
The membrane that encircles and protects the heart.

term_en: Coordination between the heart and the kidney
synonyms_en: Coordination between water and fire/harmony; between the heart and the kidney
definition: The coordinated balance between ascending heart fire (yang) and descending kidney water (yin).

term_en: Disharmony between the heart and the kidney
synonyms_en: Lack of coordination between water and fire
definition: The disharmony between ascending heart fire (yang) and descending kidney water (yin).
The qi stored in the lung. It is the driving force of physiological activities of the lung.
The yin essence of the lung, as opposed to lung yang. It refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the lung’s function.
The yang qi of the lung, as opposed to lung yin. It refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspect of the lung’s function.
A functional system composed of the lung, large intestine, skin, body hair, nose and lung meridian.
It refers to the lung. The lung is the root of the qi of the entire body.

synonyms_en: The office of the prime minister
definition: It refers to the lung. The lung governs qi and assists the heart to circulate blood; therefore, the lung is compared to the prime minister of a government.
The lung dominates respiration and the qi of the entire body.
The lung dominates breathing in the clean qi and breathing out the stale qi.

term_en: The lung governs upward and outward diffusion
definition: This refers to the upward and outward diffusion of lung qi.

term_en: The lung governs descent and purification
definition: This refers to the downward and inward depuration of lung qi.
The lung regulates water circulation and metabolism through dispersing and descending of lung qi.
It refers to the lung. The lung is located on the highest position among other zang–fu organs. It regulates water metabolism of the body.
The lung regulates waterways through the diffusion of lung qi.
pinyin: fèi zhǔ tōng diáo shuǐ dào

term_en: The lung presides over the hundred vessels
definition: The lung presides over vessels of the whole body to assist the heart’s function in circulating blood. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: The lung governs management and regulation
definition: The lung manages and regulates physiological activities of the entire body.

term_en: The lung governs the skin and body hair
synonyms_en: The lung is connected with the skin and body hair
definition: The lung warms and nourishes the skin and body hair, regulates the opening and closing of the sweat pores and safeguards the surface of the body.

term_en: The outer aspect of the lung is the skin
definition: The skin is associated with the lung.

term_en: The lustre of the lung shows in the body hair
definition: The colour and lustre of the body hair manifest the functioning of the lung.

term_en: The lung opens into the nose
definition: The nose is the opening of the lung.

term_en: The emotion of the lung is grief
definition: Grief is associated with the lung.

term_en: The fluid of the lung is nasal discharge
definition: Nasal discharge is associated with the lung.

term_en: The Lung stores the Corporeal Soul (Po)
definition: The lung helps to maintain the instinctive perception and immediate reactivity.
The lung is intolerant of cold and connected with the skin and body hair. Lung qi is easily damaged by exogenous pathogenic cold.

term_en: The pairing between the lung and large intestine
definition: The lung is internally–externally paired with the large intestine through meridians.
The qi stored in the spleen. It is the driving force of physiological activities of the spleen.
The yin essence of the spleen, as opposed to spleen yang. It refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the spleen’s function.
The yang qi of the spleen, is opposite to spleen yin. It refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspect of the spleen’s function.
A functional system composed of the spleen, stomach, muscle, lips, mouth and spleen meridian.
Refers to the spleen. The spleen transports and transforms nutrients from water and food (i.e. the essential material foundation to maintain vital activities).
Refers to the spleen. The spleen transports and transforms nutrients from water and food. It is compared to an officer of the granaries.

term_en: The spleen governs transportation and transformation
definition: A collective term used to describe the spleen’s functions in transporting and transforming water, food and fluids. The spleen digests water and food, absorbs and distributes nutrients and regulates water metabolism.
The spleen qi controls the blood to circulate within small vessels.
Opposite to the“stomach descends the turbid”, the spleen qi ascends and distributes nutrients to the heart and lungs, and maintains normal positions of the internal organs.
The spleen distributes nutrients of water and food to the four limbs to maintain their normal activities.
The spleen distributes nutrients of water and food to muscles to maintain their normal activities.

term_en: The spleen governs the four seasons
definition: There are four seasons in one year. The spleen is associated with the last 18 days in each season.

term_en: The lustre of the spleen shows in the lips
definition: The colour and lustre of the lips manifest the functioning of the spleen.

term_en: The spleen opens into the mouth
definition: The spleen receives water and food from the mouth and the mouth is the opening of the spleen.

term_en: The emotion of the spleen is overthinking
definition: The spleen is associated with thoughtfulness. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: The fluid of the spleen is thin saliva
definition: Thin saliva is associated with the spleen.
The spleen assists the heart in mental/thinking activities.
The spleen is intolerant of dampness. As an earth organ, the spleen is intolerant and affected by dampness.

term_en: The pairing between the spleen and stomach
definition: The spleen is externally–internally paired with the spleen through meridians.
The qi stored in the liver, as opposed to liver blood. It is the driving force of physiological activities of the liver.
The blood stored in the liver, as opposed to liver qi. It is the material foundation of physiological activities of the liver.
The yin essence of the liver, as opposed to liver yang. It refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the liver’s functions.
The yang qi of the liver, as opposed to liver yin. It refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspect of the liver’s functions.
A functional system composed of the liver, gallbladder, tendons, nails and liver meridian.

term_en: The liver is the foundation for fatigue endurance
definition: Refers to the liver. The liver stores blood, and the blood nourishes tendons/sinew and helps to endure fatigue.
Refers to the liver. The liver is resolute and helps with developing and planning strategies. It is compared to an army general.

term_en: The liver governs the free flow of qi
definition: The liver maintains free flow of qi over the entire body.
The liver helps with developing and planning strategies.
The liver stores blood, regulates blood volume and prevents bleeding.

term_en: The liver governs ascending and dispersing
definition: The physiological feature of the liver in the free ascending of yang qi.

term_en: The liver is the resolute organ
definition: As the resolute organ, the liver likes free will; liver yang (qi) is susceptible to becoming hyperactive.

term_en: The liver likes free will and hates to be suppressed
definition: The liver is an organ of wind and wood. Liver qi needs to be soft and unobstructed. Free flow of qi guarantees its normal physiological functions.
pinyin: gān xǐ tiáo dá ér wù yì yù

term_en: The emotion of the liver is anger
definition: Anger is associated with the liver.

term_en: The tissue of the liver is sinew
definition: Sinews are associated with the liver.

term_en: Nails are the extension of sinews
definition: Nails, as the extension of sinews, are nourished by liver blood.

term_en: The lustre of the liver shows in the nails
definition: The colour and lustre of the nails manifest the functioning of the liver.

term_en: The liver opens into the eyes
definition: The eyes are nourished by liver qi and blood and therefore the opening orifice of the liver.

term_en: The fluid of the liver are tears
definition: Tears are associated with the liver.

term_en: The liver stores the Ethereal Soul (Hun)
definition: The liver has the ability to help the heart in making strategic plans and balancing caution and courage.
The liver is intolerant of wind. It is associated with wood and susceptible to being affected by wind.

term_en: The pairing between the liver and gallbladder
definition: The liver is paired externally–internally with the gallbladder through meridians.
The liver is a yin organ because it stores (yin) blood; however, it maintains the free flow of qi (yang). 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: Liver and kidney share the same source
synonyms_en: Yi (liver) and Gui (kidney) share the same source
definition: The liver stores blood and the kidney stores essence, blood and essence can mutually transform into each other. The liver belongs to Yi (the second heavenly stems) wood, while the kidney belongs to Gui (the twelfth heavenly stems) water.
The essence stored in the kidney. It is inherited from one’s parents and nourished by water and food. It is known as the foundation of physiological activities of the kidney.
Transformed by kidney essence, it is the driving force of physiological activities of the kidney.
The yin essence of the kidney. Opposite to kidney yang, it refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the kidney’s functions.
Opposite to kidney yin, it refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspects of the kidney’s functions.
A functional system composed of the kidney, urinary bladder, bones, hair, ears, urethra, anus, and kidney meridian.
Refers to the kidney. The kidney essence inherited from parents is fundamental to the growth and reproduction.

term_en: The foundation of sealing and storing
definition: Refers to the kidney. The kidney stores and secures essential qi, absorbs clean qi, and holds urine in the urinary bladder.
Refers to the kidney. The kidney stores essence, generates marrow, and dominates bones. It is associated with the ability to do and strive, and therefore, compared to an organ of strenous work.
The kidney stores and secures the essence of human body.
The function of kidney essence and qi in boosting the maturity of reproductive organs and maintaining reproductive ability.
A material substance transformed and generated by abundant kidney essence. Tian Gui boosts the maturity of reproductive organs and maintains the reproductive function.
The kidney receives and holds the clear qi inhaled by the lung to maintain the depth of breathing.

term_en: The kidney governs water and fluids
definition: The kidney governs and regulates water metabolism.

synonyms_en: The kidney governs storing and sealing
definition: The kidney seals, stores and keeps essence within the body.
The kidney essence generates marrow to nourish bones.

term_en: Teeth are the extension of the bone
definition: The teeth and the bones share the same source – kidney essence.
The kidney essence transforms into and generates bone marrow.

term_en: The lustre of the kidney shows in the hair
definition: The colour and lustre of hair manifest the functioning of the kidney.

term_en: The kidney opens into the ears
definition: The ears are nourished by kidney essence and qi and are the opening orifice of the kidney.

term_en: The kidney opens into the urethra and anus
definition: The kidney secures essence and dominates the urethra and anus. The urethra and anus are the opening orifices of the kidney.
pinyin: shèn kāi qiào yú èr yīn

term_en: The emotion of the kidney is fear
definition: Fear is associated with the kidney.

term_en: The fluid of the kidney is thick saliva
definition: Thick saliva is associated with the kidney.
The kidney assists the heart in governing willpower and memory. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
The kidney is intolerant of dryness. The kidney stores essence and dominates body fluids. Dryness may damage yin fluids and impair kidney essence.

term_en: The pairing between the kidney and urinary bladder
definition: The kidney is internally–externally paired with the urinary bladder through meridians.
The vital qi between two kidneys. It is the origin of the qi of life.
The root of life and origin of qi transformation. It is closely associated with the functions of the kidney.

term_en: The fire of the gate of life
definition: Opposite to the water of life gate, it refers to the warming, impelling and qi transformation function of kidney yang.

term_en: The water of the gate of life
definition: Opposite to the fire of life gate, it refers to the cooling, moistening, quiescent and nourishing function of kidney yin.
Refers to the gallbladder. The gallbladder stores bile.
The essential qi of gallbladder. It secretes and discharges bile and dominates decision-making.

synonyms_en: The office of impartiality and rectitude
definition: Refers to the gallbladder. The gallbladder is involved with judgment and decision-making. It is therefore compared to the role of justice.
The gallbladder helps with judgment and decision-making ability.
Refers to the stomach. The stomach decomposes water and food. Stomach qi nourishes all five zang and six fu organs.
A collective term for the stomach organ. Its upper duct includes cardia; the lower duct includes pylorus; and between is the middle duct.
Qi of the stomach or of the spleen and stomach, coupled with their physiological functions.
The yang qi of the stomach, as opposed to stomach yin. It refers to the activating, impelling and warming aspect of the stomach’s function.
The yin essence of the stomach, as opposed to stomach yang. It refers to the quiescent and moistening aspect of the stomach’s function.

term_en: The stomach governs receiving and holding
definition: The stomach receives and holds the water and food.
The stomach primarily digests water and food and forms chyme.
Stomach qi needs to be unobstructed and flows downward, so as to pass the primarily digested chyme down to the small intestine.
Stomach qi descends the initially digested chyme to the small intestine and eliminates the waste from the body.

term_en: The stomach likes softening and moisturizing
definition: In five-element theory the stomach is a fu organ and associated with the earth. It is dry in nature and its normal functioning relies on the moistening of yin fluids.

synonyms_en: The office of receiving and holding
definition: Refers to the small intestine. The small intestine receives the chyme from the stomach and separates the clear (useful substances) from the turbid (wastes). It is therefore compared to a receptacle or container.

term_en: The small intestine governs receiving and holding
definition: The small intestine receives and holds the decomposed water and food.
The small intestine further digests the water and food, absorbs nutrients and passes the waste down to the large intestine. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: The small intestine governs thick body fluids
definition: The small intestine further absorbs the nutrients while separating the clear from the turbid.

term_en: The small intestine separates the clear from the turbid
definition: The small intestine absorbs nutrients and body fluids and passes the food residue and water down to the large intestine.
pinyin: xiǎo cháng mì bié qīng zhuó

definition: Refers to the large intestine, since it eliminates the waste out of the body.
The large intestine conducts wastes and discharges faeces.

term_en: The large intestine governs the thin body fluids
definition: The large intestine absorbs the thin, clear fluids while eliminating waste.
Refers to the urinary bladder – the organ in charge of the water in the three jiao.

term_en: Qi transformation of the urinary bladder
definition: The bladder relies on kidney qi transformation to store and excrete urine.

synonyms_en: The office of dredging and draining
definition: Refers to sanjiao – the water passage within the human body. Its function is compared to someone who is responsible for dredging a ditch.
A fu organ. A collective term for upper jiao, middle jiao and lower jiao. It serves as a pathway for qi and water circulation and dominates qi transformation.
The upper jiao is located above the diaphragm and includes the heart and lung.
The middle jiao is located between the diaphragm and navel and includes the spleen, stomach, liver and gallbladder.
The lower jiao is located below the navel and includes the kidney, urinary bladder, large intestine, and small intestine.
The heart and lung distribute qi and blood. Their function is compared with the permeation of mist and dew.
The spleen and stomach decompose water and food. Their function is compared to fermentation.
The kidney and urinary bladder regulate water discharge. Their function is compared to an unobstructed ditch.

term_en: The house of the original spirit
definition: Refers to the brain – the source of mental activities.
Refers to the head – a place where the spirit, qi, essence and marrow converge.
An extraordinary organ. A collective term for brain marrow, spinal cord and bone marrow. Marrow is transformed from kidney essence.
An extraordinary organ that stores bone marrow, supports the body, protects the internal organs, and helps with body movements.
An extraordinary organ, referring to the pathway for qi and blood circulation.

term_en: Hair is the extension of blood
definition: The growth of hair depends on the nourishment of blood.
An extraordinary organ. A collective term for female internal genital organs.

synonyms_en: The office of the servant and messenger
definition: It refers to the pericardium that acts to protect the heart against exogenous pathogenic factors.
All tangible nutrients of the human body. It can also specifically refer to the kidney essence.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The intangible, high-mobility nutritive substance that maintains vital activities. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The red liquid that circulates within the blood vessels to moisten and nourish the body. It is an essential substance to maintain life activities.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: A collective term for thinner part of fluids (jin) and thicker part of liquid (ye). Body fluids are essential to maintain life activities.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

synonyms_en: Pre-heaven essence; prenatal essence; congenital essence
definition: The original substance of life inherited from one’s parents and contributed to the generation of offspring.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The nutritive substances obtained through qi transformation of the zang–fu organs after birth.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: A collective term for essence and qi. It serves as the fundamental substance of the human body and maintains vital activities.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: A general term referring to various changes generated by qi movement. All things in the universe are transformed by qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Qi movement can be classified into four basic forms, namely ascending, descending, exiting and entering.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: A collective term for qi of the entire body, including innate qi and acquired qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

synonyms_en: Pre-heaven qi; prenatal qi; congenital qi
definition: The qi inherited from one’s parents and stored in the kidney.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The qi transformed from the essential qi of water and food as well as the clean qi (fresh air inhaled in the lung) of the nature.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Rooted in the kidney, Yuan-primordial qi consists of innate essence qi and Ying-nutrients qi transformed from water and food. It includes primordial yin qi and primordial yang qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The qi that accumulates in the chest. It consists of clean qi (fresh air inhaled in the lung) in the nature and qi transformed from water and food.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Opposite to Wei-defensive qi. Ying-nutrients qi is transformed from water and food and travels within the blood vessels.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The qi within blood and yin within qi. When used in combination with blood, it often represents yin blood. Alternatively, it generally refers to blood.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Ying-nutrient is yin and flexible in nature and travels within the vessels.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Opposite to the Ying-nutrient qi. It travels outside the vessels and is transformed from the nutrients of water and food.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Wei-defence is yang and resolute in nature. It travels outside the vessels.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The qi stored in the zang–fu organs and maintains normal physiological functions of the zang–fu organs.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: It is also known as qi of the spleen and stomach.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The qi circulates within the meridians and falls under the category of healthy qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The basic forms of qi movement.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Qi has the function of warming the body.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Blood has the function of nourishing and moistening the body.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The thin, clear and high-mobility body fluids that distribute over the skin, muscles or orifices and permeates into blood vessels. This part of fluids moistens the body. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The thick, low-mobility body fluids that perfuse into the bones, joints, zang–fu organs, brain and marrows. This part of fluids nourishes the body and lubricates the bones/joints.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

term_en: Qi is the commander of the blood
definition: This refers to the functions of qi in transforming, circulating and governing blood.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Qi can transform into blood. Blood is transformed from nutrients from water and food and Ying- nutrient qi within the blood vessels.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The heart qi, lung qi and liver qi maintain the normal circulation of blood.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

synonyms_en: Qi holds blood; Qi contains blood
definition: This refers to the normal functioning of spleen qi and liver qi in keeping the blood circulating within the blood vessels.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

term_en: Blood is the mother of qi
definition: Blood transforms into and carries qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The function of tangible blood in carrying intangible qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Qi of the zang–fu organs transforms into and engenders body fluids.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: Qi of the zang–fu organs promotes the normal distribution of body fluids.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

synonyms_en: Qi holds body fluids; qi contains body fluids
definition: Qi keeps the body fluid within the waterways and maintains its normal circulation.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The function of tangible body fluids in carrying intangible qi.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

term_en: Body fluids and blood share the same source
definition: Body fluids and blood are both transformed from nutrients found in water and food; the two mutually generate each other.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

term_en: Essence and blood share the same source
definition: Essence qi and blood are both transformed from nutrients of water and food; the two mutually generate each other.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

term_en: Blood and sweat share the same source
definition: Since blood is composed of body fluids and Ying- nutrient qi and sweat is transformed from body fluids, the blood and sweat share the same source.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The normal fire that benefits growth.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: The normal fire generates the Yuan-primordial qi and maintains vital activities.
category_en: Essence, qi, blood and body fluids

definition: All causes of diseases.

term_en: To differentiate pattern to reveal an etiology
definition: A method to seek the etiological factors according to clinical manifestations.
A theory that classifies etiological factors into internal, external and neither internal nor external.
These mainly refer to seven emotional disturbances.
These mainly refer to six exogenous pathogenic factors.

term_en: Neither internal nor external etiological factors
definition: Pathogenic factors that are not categorized as external or internal, such as improper diet, over- exertion, traumatic injuries, animal/insect bites, drowning etc.
Pathogenic factors that attack the body through the skin, mouth and nose, including six pathogenic factors and epidemic qi.
Internal dysfunctions due to extreme emotions, over-exertion, and improper diet.
Opposite to healthy qi, it is a collective term for all pathogenic factors.
Opposite to yin pathogens, refers to pathogenic factors of yang nature, such as wind, summer-heat or fire-heat.
Opposite to yang pathogens, refers to pathogenic factors of yin nature, such as cold or dampness. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

Opposite to excess pathogens, it is a collective term for exogenous pathogenic factors that invade the body when the body is weak. Alternatively, it refers to pathogenic qi that transmits from the mother organ to the son organ.
Opposite to deficiency pathogens, it is a collective term for pathogenic factors. Alternatively, it refers to pathogenic qi that transmits from the son organ to the mother organ.
A collective term for epidemic, etiological factors associated with the four seasons.
External pathogenic factors that damage the human body.
A collective term for six exogenous pathogenic factors: wind, cold, summer-heat, dampness, dryness and fire.
A collective term for exogenous pathogenic factors with high contagiousness.
A pathogenic factor with high contagiousness.
Seven normal emotions include joy, anger, anxiety, overthinking, grief, fear and fright.
A collective term for damage caused by extreme emotions including joy, anger, anxiety, overthinking, grief, fear and fright.
Fire pattern transformed from disturbance of joy, anger, grief, overthinking and fear.
Diet harmful to health, including unhealthy dietary habits, ingestion of contaminated food, dietary preference, etc.
A collective term for over-exertion and physical inactivity.
A pathogenic factor that induces or aggravates medical conditions by errors of health care professionals.
Harm to the body by animals or insects.
A pathogenic factor characterized by opening the skin pores, high mobility and upward/outward movement.
Wind loosens the interspace between skin/muscle fibers and opens the skin pores, resulting in sweating and aversion to wind.
Wind is characterized by upward flowing. It easily affects the head, face, surface of the body and yang meridians.
Wind is characterized by constant moving. It causes the limbs to tremble.
Wind is characterised by swift changes. Diseases caused by wind are marked by a sudden onset of symptoms in moving locations.

term_en: Wind is the leading cause of diseases
synonyms_en: Wind is the spearhead of a hundred diseases
definition: Wind may cause a wide variety of conditions. It is the spearhead of exogenous pathogenic factors and liable to associate itself with cold, dampness, dryness and heat.
pinyin: fēng wéi bǎi bìng zhī zhǎng

definition: A pathogenic factor characterized by coldness, stagnation, congealing and contraction.
Cold is yin in nature and can easily impair yang qi.
Pathogenic cold causes qi/blood to stagnate, blocks meridians, and causes pain.
Pathogenic cold constricts qi, blocks the skin pores, and causes contractions.
A pathogenic factor commonly seen between the summer solstice and beginning of autumn. It is characterized by flames ascending and dispersing.
Pathogenic summer heat is characterized by extreme hotness. Often causes hyperactive yang heat. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
Summer heat ascends and disperses. Often directly affects the qi phase, opens the sweating pores and damages body fluids.

term_en: Summer heat often combines with dampness
definition: Summer is hot, humid and rainy. The summer heat provokes dampness and is often liable to mix itself with dampness.
A pathogenic factor that obstructs the flow of qi. It is characterized by heaviness, turbidity, stickiness and downward flowing.
Dampness is a tangible pathogenic factor and is easy to obstruct qi movement.
Dampness is yin in nature and can easily damage yang qi. It is tangible and can obstruct the flow of yang qi.
Pathogenic dampness is characterized by its heaviness and turbidity. The diseases caused by it may lead to heaviness of the body and turbidity of secretions and excrements.
Dampness is characterized by stickiness and stagnation. It causes sticky, viscous secretions and discharges. Dampness-induced conditions often last a long time.
Dampness move downward and affects the yin and lower parts of the body.
A pathogenic factor that consumes body fluids and tends to damage the lung.
Dryness desiccates by consuming body fluids and causing body fluid deficiency and lack of moisture.
Dryness invades the body through the nose, mouth and skin pores. It easily damages the lung fluids and impairs the dispersing of lung qi.
A pathogenic factor that flames upward, consumes qi and body fluids, engenders wind, stirs blood, and harasses the heart spirit.
A pathogenic factor that causes excessive pathological changes of hot and yang nature.
A collective term for pathogenic warm heat, including spring warmth, wind warmth, summer heat warmth, damp warmth, autumn dryness, winter warmth, pestilence warmth, warm toxin, warm malaria, etc.
Toxic pathogens include toxins transformed from six exogenous pathogenic factors, toxic fire from sores/ulcers, toxic heat, snake venom, rabies or toxic lacquer.
The nature of pathogenic fire flames upward. It causes heat symptoms and often affects the upper part of the body.
Fire tends to stir liver wind. Extreme heat can cause stirring of wind.
Since fire may burn the vessels and collaterals and cause the blood to move recklessly, it often results in bleeding or macular eruption.

term_en: Fire consumes qi and body fluids
definition: Since fire consumes healthy qi and scorches yin fluids, it often causes deficiency of both qi and thin fluids.

term_en: Fire tends to disturb the heart spirit
synonyms_en: Fire tends to disturb the heart Shen
definition: Since fire tends to disturb the heart spirit, it often causes mental restlessness.
Since fire heat tends to enter the blood and remain in a fixed location, it often causes sores/ ulcers.
Hyperactive, pathogenic fire that consumes healthy qi.

Excessive anger damages liver qi, impairs the function of liver in maintaining the free flow of qi, causes the qi to rise, and results in disordered qi and blood. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
Excessive joy damages heart spirit, consumes heart qi and results in mental derangement.
Excessive overthinking damages spleen qi, causes qi to stagnate, and impairs the function of the spleen in transportation and transformation.
Excessive grief damages and consumes lung qi and impairs the dispersal of lung qi.
Excessive fear damages kidney qi, causes kidney qi to descend, and impairs the function of the kidney in storing essence.
Improper diet, including excessive hunger and binge eating.
Intake of contaminated or poisonous food.
Excessive indulgence in specific food, including cold or hot food, certain flavours or alcohol.
The five flavours are spicy, sweet, sour, bitter and salty. Habitual preference for a particular flavour or taste may bring about adverse reactions or damage the five zang organs.
Overwork can be physical, mental or sexual.
Excessive physical activities damage the zang–fu organs and cause qi deficiency of the zang organs.
Excessive mental activities tend to damage heart blood and spleen qi.
Excessive sexual activities consume and damage kidney essence.
Physical inactivity leads to imbalances in the flow of qi and blood, weak tendons and bones, stagnant qi of the spleen and stomach. In severe cases, it may even cause other secondary diseases.

The five exhaustions are listed as follows: Long- time observation damages blood; long-time lying damages qi; long-time sitting damages muscles; long-time standing damages bones; and long-time walking damages sinews. Alternatively, the five overstrains refer to deficiencies of the five zang organs (i.e. liver, heart, spleen, lung and kidney).
A collective term for stagnation of qi, blood, phlegm, fire, food and dampness. Often results from qi stagnation of the liver and spleen.

Refers to the seven pathogenic factors that lead to deficiency and consumption, including improper diet, anxiety, drink, sex, hunger, over-exertion, and damage to meridians, collaterals, Ying-nutrients, Wei-defense and qi.

Associated with fluid retention. It refers to the viscous, turbid pathological products that accumulate in the body due to disordered water metabolism. It can be an etiological factor for a variety of diseases.
Tangible phlegm is visible, touchable and audible when it is secreted from the airways.
Intangible phlegm is invisible and impalpable; however, it can cause pathogenic features of phlegm.

The spleen governs transportation and transformation of water and food. The failure of the spleen to transport and transform water fluids may cause internal retention of water dampness and generate phlegm.

The lung dominates water and regulates the water passage. The failure of the lung to disperse qi may cause internal retention of phlegm fluids. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

Fluid retention is relative to phlegm. It refers to the thin, clear pathological products that accumulate in the body due to disordered water metabolism. It can also be an etiological factor for a variety of diseases.
Fluid retention that lasts a long period of time. It is one type of fluid retention.
A type of fluid retention that is deeply located and hard to remove.
A pathological product formed during slow blood flow or as blood coagulates. It is also a secondary pathogenic factor.
The gravel-like substance that accumulates in the human body, especially in the ducts and cavities of zang–fu organs. It is also a secondary pathogenic factor.
An inherited etiological factor that transmits the body constitution and disease of the mother to her fetus.
A pre-birth toxin. It is a pathogenic factor that causes infantile skin rashes.
A collective term for a congenitally weak constitution and a deficiency of qi and blood. It is a major contributing factor to a deficiency of healthy qi.
Congenital constitutional weakness is an internal etiological factor of healthy qi deficiency.
The five pathological states of wind, fire, cold, dryness and dampness due to dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs.

Opposite to external wind, it is a pathological state of yang qi hyperactivity and wind stirring due to disordered qi and blood of the zang–fu organs. This includes extreme heat generating wind, liver yang transforming into wind, blood deficiency generating wind and yin deficiency stirring wind.
Opposite to external cold, it is a pathological state of deficiency cold due to yang qi deficiency of the zang–fu organs.
Opposite to external dampness, it is a pathological state of retained water, dampness, phlegm and turbidity due to dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs and disordered water metabolism.
Opposite to external dryness, it is a pathological state of body fluids failing to moisten the body.
Opposite to external fire, it is a pathological state of fire heat due to disordered qi, blood, yin and yang of the zang–fu organs.
The pathogenic fire produced from improper diet, fatigue, joy, anger, grief, overthinking, qi deficiency or yang deficiency.
The mechanism of the occurrence, progress, and change of the disease.

Opposite to pathogenic factors, it is a collective term for physiological functions of the body, including the body’s ability to adapt to the external environment, defend against pathogens and recover from diseases.
Opposite to the latent pathogenic qi in the theory of warm disease, it often causes a sudden onset of disease.
Opposite to exposure to acute pathogenic qi in the theory of febrile diseases, it causes the occurrence of diseases after a period of time. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
A rapid appearance of symptoms after being in contact with a pathogen.
A gradual appearance of symptoms after being in contact with a pathogen.
Relapse of diseases due to etiological or inducing factors.
Relapse of diseases due to intake of improper diet or intake of contaminated food.
Relapse of disease due to the damage to healthy qi by overwork
A pathological state of pathogenic factors affecting two meridians that are interior–exteriorly connected.
Transmission and transformation of diseases among five zang organs.
Two or more external pathogenic factors invade the body. Alternatively, it means exogenous pathogenic factors triggering previously existing diseases.
Pathological states caused by pathogenic factors invading the mouth, nose, ears and eyes.

term_en: Struggle between anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors
definition: The struggle between healthy qi and pathogenic factors determines the pathogenic nature of diseases. Alternatively, it is specifically used to explain the pathogenesis of alternating fever and chills in Shaoyang disease due to cold damage.

term_en: Waxing and waning of anti-pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors
definition: The pathological states due to the struggle between healthy qi and pathogenic factors.
Opposite to deficiency, it is a hyperactive pathological state due to a fierce struggle between excessive pathogenic factors and normal healthy qi.
Opposite to excess, it is a hypoactive pathological state due to the struggle between weak healthy qi and mild/moderate pathogenic factors.
A pathological state due to deficiency of healthy qi and excess of pathogenic factors. This includes deficiency complicated with excess and excess complicated with deficiency.
A pathological state that mainly manifests as a deficiency of healthy qi, accompanied by excessive pathogenic factors.
A pathological state that mainly manifests as excess of pathogenic factors, accompanied by a deficiency of healthy qi.

term_en: True or false deficiency and excess
definition: The false symptoms contrary to the true nature of the disease. This includes true deficiency with false excess and true excess with false deficiency.
The false excess symptoms due to extreme deficiency of healthy qi.
The false deficiency symptoms due to extreme excess of pathogenic factors.
The mutual transformation between deficiency of healthy qi and excess of pathogenic factors. This includes excess transforming into deficiency and deficiency into excess.
A transformation from an excess pattern (hyperactivity of pathogenic factors) to a deficiency pattern (deficiency of healthy qi).
A transformation from a deficiency pattern (deficiency of healthy qi) to an excess pattern (hyperactivity of pathogenic factors). 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

A general term for pathological states due to waxing and waning of yin and yang. This includes excess of yin or yang, deficiency of yin or yang, mutual impairment between yin and yang, rejection between yin and yang, transformation between yin and yang, and depletion/loss of yin or yang.
Pathological states due to excess of yin or yang.
Coexisting yin waxing and yang waning. Over time, excess yin cold may damage yang qi and result in yang depletion.
Mutual restraint between yin and yang maintains relative yin–yang equilibrium. The failure of yang to restrain yin may cause relative yin excess.
Coexisting yang waxing and yin waning. Often develops when waxing yang severely damages yin; however, yin damage is more severe.

term_en: When yang prevails, yin fluids will be consumed.
definition: A pathological state of overwhelming yang heat consuming yin fluids.
A pathological state of overwhelming yang leading to excess heat.

term_en: When yin prevails, yang qi will be impaired.
definition: A pathological state of excess yin cold consuming yang qi.
A pathological state of overwhelming yin leading to excess cold.
Pathological states due to deficiency of yin or yang.
A pathological state of yang qi deficiency leading to deficiency cold.
A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang and deficiency heat.

term_en: Yin deficiency leading to yang hyperactivity
definition: A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang.

term_en: Yin deficiency leading to fire hyperactivity
definition: A pathological state in which yin fluid fails to control yang and causes a relative hyperactivity of yang and deficiency fire.

term_en: Mutual impairment between yin and yang
definition: A pathological state of deficiency of both yin and yang. Often results from severe deficiency of yin affecting yang or vice versa. This includes yin deficiency affecting yang and yang deficiency affecting yin.
A pathological state in which yang qi deficiency impedes the generation of yin, resulting in deficiency of both yin and yang with a preponderance of yang deficiency.
A pathological state in which consumption of yin affects yang qi, resulting in deficiency of both yin and yang with a preponderance of yin deficiency.

term_en: Dual deficiency of yin and yang
definition: A pathological state of coexisting yin deficiency and yang deficiency.

A serious pathological state in which extremely excessive yin in the interior forces the deficient yang to spread outward or extremely excessive yang in the interior keeps deficient yin on the outside, forming pseudo-heat or pseudo-cold. This includes excessive yin rejecting yang and excessive yang rejecting yin.
A pathological state of true cold with false heat when interior yin cold due to extreme yang deficiency forces the deficient yang to float on the exterior of the body.

A pathological state of true heat with false cold when interior yang heat blocks the movement of qi and forces the yin to float on the exterior of the body. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
A pathological state of upward floating of yang qi due to excessive yin rejecting yang or loss/ consumption of essence blood.
A critical state of sudden, heavy loss of yin fluid or yang qi. This includes yin collapse and yang collapse.
A critical state of massive loss and sudden failure of yin fluid.
A critical state of massive loss and sudden failure of yang qi.
A pathological state of exhaustion of yin fluid and loss of yang qi.
A critical state of separation between yin and yang due to extreme deficiency of yin and yang.
Disordered activity of qi in ascending, descending, entering and exiting. It may cause qi stagnation, adverse qi flow, qi sinking, qi blockage and qi exhaustion.

A general term for dysfunctions of the zang–fu organs. It is often used to explain dysfunctions of qi of the zang–fu organs in ascending the clear and descending the turbid. It may cause hiccups, chest stuffiness, abdominal distension/pain and irregular bowel/bladder movements.
A pathological state of decreased zang–fu functions or body weakness due to deficiency of qi.
A pathological state in which extreme deficiency of qi causes qi to float on the exterior of the body.
A pathological state in which qi is obstructed inside.
A pathological state of reversed upflow of qi. Either excessive upward flow of qi or inhibited downward flow of qi.
A pathological state in which qi fails to lift or hold but flows downward.
A pathological state in which the movement of qi is inhibited.
Stagnant movement of qi. It is often associated with emotions and disorder of qi and blood. Often refers to liver qi stagnation.
A pathological state of prolonged qi stagnation transforming into fire heat.
A pathological state in which deficient blood fails to nourish the zang–fu organs and meridians/ channels.
A pathological state of slow, coagulated or stagnant circulation of blood.
A pathological state in which cold enters the blood phase and causes the blood to stagnate or coagulate.
A pathological state in which heat enters the blood phase and causes the blood to move recklessly.

term_en: Blood failing to flow within the vessels
definition: A pathological state in which blood moves recklessly out of the vessels.

term_en: Blood failing to nourish the sinews
definition: A pathological state in which liver blood fails to nourish the sinews and causes muscle/tendon spasm.
Any failure in the mutually coordinating relationship between qi and blood.

term_en: Dual deficiency of qi and blood
definition: A pathological state of malnourishment of the body or weakened bodily function due to simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and blood deficiency.
A pathological state in which the dysfunction of qi affects the blood and causes blood deficiency, stagnant blood or bleeding. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: Reckless flow of blood due to heat
definition: A pathological state of bleeding due to heat in the blood stirring or consuming blood and forcing it out of the vessels.

term_en: Qi collapse following loss of thick fluids
definition: A critical state in which a massive loss of bodily fluids causes sudden collapse/loss of yang qi.

term_en: Qi failing to transform thin fluids
definition: A pathological state in which yang qi fails to vaporize water and perform qi transformation.

term_en: Water retention obstructing the flow of qi
definition: A pathological state in which retained water within the body impedes the qi ascending, descending and transformation of the zang–fu organs.

term_en: Blood stasis due to qi stagnation
definition: A pathological state in which stagnant qi affects the circulation of blood and causes simultaneous presence of qi stagnation and blood stasis.

term_en: Blood stasis due to qi deficiency
definition: A pathological state in which qi fails to promote the circulation of blood and causes blood stasis, resulting in simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and blood stasis.
A pathological state in which qi fails to contain blood and allows the blood to flow out of the vessels.

term_en: Qi collapse following heavy blood loss
definition: A critical state in which massive blood loss causes sudden collapse of qi.
A pathological state in which upward adverse flow of qi leads to blood rushing upward and results in haematemesis, haemoptysis or stroke.
A pathological state in which the thin, clear fluids are consumed.
A pathological state of emaciation and functional failures of the zang–fu organs. Alternatively, it can be a life-threatening sign due to major consumption of heavy, thick fluids.

term_en: Fluid exhaustion leading to blood dryness
definition: A pathological state in which fluids fail to supplement blood and causes blood dryness and internal dry heat.

term_en: Dual deficiency of qi and yin
definition: A pathological state of simultaneous presence of qi deficiency and yin deficiency.

term_en: The water gate failing to operate
definition: A pathological state in which dysfunctions of the kidney in qi transformation causes inhibited urination (dysuria) and oedema.

A pathological state of yin–yang disharmony and hyperactive yang transforming into fire. Alternatively, it occurs when prolonged intake of pungent, warm-property aphrodisiacs generates internal fire toxins and consumes essence qi.

term_en: Disharmony between the Ying-nutrients and Wei-defence
definition: A pathological state of lack of coordination between the Ying-nutritive qi and Wei-defensive qi.
A pathological state of spontaneous sweating without fever due to deficiency of the Wei- defensive qi (in an exterior pattern).
A pathological state of sweating that occurs only during fever in an exterior pattern.

synonyms_en: Frenetic stirring of the ministerial fire
definition: A pathological state of upward flame of fire due to yin deficiency of the liver and kidney. Common symptoms may include dizziness, headache, blurred vision, tinnitus, deafness, irritability, dream-disturbed sleep, feverish sensations in the palms, soles and chest, hypersexuality, nocturnal emissions, premature ejaculations, etc.
The activities to maintain physical and mental health and prevent illnesses.
The congenital life expectancy

term_en: Preventing a disease before it arises
definition: A concept to prevent a disease before it arises and prevents transmission of a disease after its onset. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

term_en: Preventing a disease before it arises
definition: A method to strengthen the healthy qi and eliminate potential harmful factors to prevent the occurrence of a disease.

term_en: Preventing transmission of a disease after its onset
definition: A method to use early diagnosis and early intervention to prevent disease progression and transmission.

term_en: Protecting yang in spring and summer
definition: Yang qi rises and grows in the spring and the summer. It is necessary to protect and nourish the internal yang qi to keep it sufficient along with the seasons.

term_en: Nourishing yin in autumn and winter
definition: Everything is stored in the autumn and the winter. It is necessary to protect and store the internal yin essence to keep it internally accumulated along with the seasons.
The physical appearance and the mental activities are inseparable. The robust physical appearance and sound vitality is the sign of body–mind wellness.

term_en: Regulating spirit according to four seasonal qi
definition: The adjustment of mental activities along with the climate of four seasons.

A collective name of wood movement, fire movement, earth movement, metal movement, water movement, and the collective name of wind, summer heat (heat), dampness, dryness, fire, cold in the natural world.

The collective name of wood movement, fire movement, earth movement, metal movement, and water movement. It reflects the changes of qi of five elements between heaven and earth. Ten heavenly stems of jia, yi, bing, ding, wu, ji, geng, xin, ren, and gui are used to record the movements.

The six normal climatic phenomena of wind, summer heat (heat), dampness, dryness, fire, and cold in the natural world. The twelve earthly branches of zi, chou, yin, mou, chen, si, wu, wei, shen, you, xu, and hai are used to record the six qi.
The collective name of jia, yi, bing, ding, wu, ji, geng, xin, ren, and gui.
The collective name of zi, chou, yin, mou, chen, si, wu, wei, shen, you, xu, and hai.

The heavenly stems pair with the earthly branches, following their orders, from jia–zi to gui–hai, forming a complete cycle of sixty years. The heavenly stems initiate with jia and the earthly branches initiate with zi. The combination is used to number years, months, days and times.

The movement governs the year, being jia and ji in category of earth movement, yi and geng in category of metal movement, bing and xin in category of water movement, ding and ren in category of wood movement, and wu and gui in category of fire movement. For example, jia and ji is in category of earth movement, the movement of the year of the jia-zi year is earth.

Each of the five movements dominates in spring, summer, later summer, autumn and winter. Starting from the severe cold and following the order of generating cycle of five elements, the first movement is wood, the second is fire, the third is earth, the fourth is metal, and the fifth is water.

The special climatic changes of the five seasons. It varies in every season in every year. Starting from the movement of the year as the initial movement, calculate in five steps according to the excess and insufficiency order of five elements. Ten years is a complete cycle and covers ten heavenly stems. Ten years is a complete cycle that covers ten heavenly stems. Then the cycle starts all over agin. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

The combination of wind, cold, dampness, dryness, sovereign fire, ministerial fire with host qi in six steps. The initial qi is in association with Jueyin, wind and wood, the second qi with Shaoyin and sovereign fire, the third qi with Shaoyang and ministerial fire, and the forth qi with Taiyin, dampness and earth, the fifth qi with yang ming, dryness and metal, the sixth (final) qi with Taiyang, cold and water.

The collective name of wind, cold, dampness, dryness, sovereign fire and ministerial fire, being opposed to the guest qi. It reflects the normal seasonal climatic changes of the year. The calculation is to relate twenty four solar terms to six qi in six steps. The four solar terms consist of one step, being six steps for one year. The calculation starts from the severe cold.

1) Reflects the abnormal climatic changes of the year, being opposed to the host qi. It includes the celestial qi, the terrestrial qi, and the four right and left intervening qi. The first yin is in association with Jueyin, wind, and wood, the second yin with Shaoyin and sovereign fire, and the third yin with Taiyin, dampness, and earth. The first yang is in association with Shaoyang and ministerial fire, the second yang with yang ming, dryness, and metal, the third yang with Taiyang, cold, and water. The calculation is to combine the above yin–yang order with twelve earthly branches. 2) External pathogenic factors.
The guest qi governing the climatic changes of the first half of the year.
The guest qi governing the climatic changes of the second half of the year. It is opposite to celestial qi.
The qi left and right to the celestial qi and the qi left and right to the terrestrial qi.
The intervening qi left to the celestial qi becomes the celestial qi and the intervening qi left to the terrestrial qi becomes the terrestrial qi.
The celestial qi becomes the intervening qi right to the celestial qi and the terrestrial qi becomes the intervening qi right to the terrestrial qi.
The excess of qi is restrained and the insufficiency of qi is compensated in the five movements.
The five movements and six qi share the same category of the five elements.
The movement qi of the year and the celestial qi share the same category of the five elements in one year.
The movement qi of the year and the earthly branch of the year share the same category of the five elements in one year.
The heavenly stem and the earthly branch of the year are both yang and the movement of the year and the terrestrial qi share the same category of the five elements in one year.
The heavenly stem and the earthly branch of the year are both yin and the movement of the year and the terrestrial qi share the same category of the five elements in one year.
The movement of the year, the celestial qi, and earthly branch of the year share the same category of the five elements in one year.

term_en: Tip qi, root qi and middle qi
definition: The study of relationship between six qi of heaven and six qi of the human body. It is used to determine the principle of the treatment based on interactions between human and nature.
Six qi of heaven, being wind, heat, dampness, dryness, cold and fire.
Qi of six meridians of Shaoyang, Taiyang, Yangming, Shaoyin, Taiyin and Jueyin. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
The relationship between the prevailing qi and the retaliating qi in five movements and six qi. They coexist by increasing and decreasing in the same direction.
The qi that is stronger and restrain another qi in the five movements and six qi.
The qi that is weaker and is restrained from another qi in the five movements and six qi.
The fire in the heart. It is opposite to the ministerial fire.
The fire dwelling in the liver, gallbladder, kidney and triple energizer, being opposite to the sovereign fire.

The sum total of the knowledge, skills and practices based on the theories, beliefs and experiences indigenous to different cultures, whether explicable or not, used in the maintenance of health as well as in the prevention, diagnosis, improvement or treatment of physical and mental illness.
A comprehensive system originated in ancient China that involves the study of life, health and diseases.

synonyms_en: Basic theory of traditional Chinese medicine
definition: Rational understandings of fundamental knowledge in traditional Chinese medicine. These include essential concepts, regular patterns, theories and principles. These understandings guide the application of traditional Chinese medicine in health preservation and disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment as well as rehabilitation.
pinyin: zhōng yī jī chǔ lǐ lùn

definition: The integral entity of the human body. The integration of human beings with nature and society.
Man and nature correspond to each other.
The oneness of human beings, heaven, earth and nature.
1) Dominance of life activities. 2) Outer manifestation reflecting the life activities. 3) State of mind, mood and mental activities.
Mind or spirit. Alternatively, it also refers to all natural phenomena and patterns, including the sun, moon and stars.
Another name of the sweat pore for inflow and outflow of qi.
Another name of the sweat pore for dispersion and flowing of qi and fluid.
Refers to the striae of the skin, muscle and organs, also to the space between the skin, muscle and organs, the minute passages for the fluid percolation and the flowing of qi and blood.
A collective name of blood wheel, wind wheel, flesh wheel, qi wheel and water wheel for the eye, which is closely related to the physiological conditions or/and pathological changes.
Refers to blood vessels at the canthus of eyes, pertaining to the heart. The heart governs blood. Its disorders are related to the heart.
Refers to the black part of the eye, pertaining to the liver. The liver is the organ of wind and wood. Its disorders are related to the liver.
Refers to the eyelids, pertaining to the spleen. The spleen governs flesh. Its disorders are related to the spleen.
Refers to the white part of the eye, pertaining to the lung. The lung governs qi. Its disorders are related to the lung. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语
Refers to the pupil, pertaining to the kidney. The kidney governs water. Its disorders are related to the kidney.
Seven major places in the digestive tract, being flying gate, door gate, breathing gate, rushing gate, pylorus, screen gate and corporeal gate.
Another name for lips.
Another name for teeth.
Another name for epiglottis.
Upper opening of the stomach.
Lower opening of the stomach.
Junction between large and small intestines.
Another name for anus.
The external genitals.
Anus.
The area around the lips reflecting the strength and the weakness of the essential qi in the spleen.
The place where the male stores the essence, including testicles, epididymis, seminal vesicles and prostate. It is associated with reproduction.
1) Four limbs. 2) Distal ends of toes and fingers.
1) The gathering venue of pectoral qi, at the centre of the two nipples. 2) Another name of pericardium. 3) Name of an acupuncture point located in the midpoint between two nipples.
The major collateral of the stomach, one of the sixteen collaterals, located at the apex of heart below the left nipple, which is the gathering venue of pectoral qi.
The empty space or depression at the connection of muscles. The large one known as the“valley” and the small one as the“creek”.
A term used to refer to: 1) uterus; 2) Chong meridian; or 3) liver.

term_en: Gathering of muscle around genital region
definition: 1) Muscle regions of three yang and three yin meridians gathering at the genital regions. 2) Male external genitalia.
The space inferior to the heart and superior to the diaphragm. When used as a disease location, it often means that the condition is incurable.

There are five sense organs, namely, the tongue, nose, mouth, eyes and ears. The throat is also considered as a sense organ. There are a total of nine orifices (seven yang orifices and two yin orifices), namely, the eyes (2), ears (2), nostrils (2), mouth, anterior yin (external genitalia including the external orifice of the urethra) and posterior yin (anus).
The eyes are categorized into eight regions according to zang–fu theory to match with the eight trigrams. This helps to further categorize and differentiate patterns of eye disease.
The white opaque part of the outer surface of the eyeball, i.e. the conjunctiva and sclera.

The transparent membranous structure forming the central anterior part of the eye, i.e. the cornea. Since this part corresponds to the liver, corneal eye problems are often associated with the liver and gallbladder. 1 Fundamentals of traditional Chinese medicine 一、中医基础理论术语

In a narrow sense, it refers to the opening at the centre of the iris, posterior to the cornea, through which light enters the eye. In a broad sense, it refers to the pupil and all attached tissues. Since this part corresponds to the kidney (the water wheel according to the five-wheel theory) and the liver and kidney share the same source, pupil- related eye problems are often associated with the liver and kidney.
Tears and transparent, watery fluid secreted from the ciliary epithelium.
The clear, colourless gel that fills the space between the lens and the retina of the eyeball.
An ancient term for the nose. It also refers to the chart of the twelve meridians and points in Chinese medicine.
1) An exogenous pathogenic factor. 2) Special odour of the patients’body, excretion and secretion. 3) Pathological products steamed by damp heat.
synonyms_zh: 二、诊断、病证和体质术语

definition: Abnormal functions reflecting the presence of an unusual state, or of a disease. It includes a patient’s subjective feelings or manifestations perceived by a doctor.
Abnormal changes that can be objectively measured.
A pathological summarization on the disease location, etiological factors, nature, severity and prognosis in a certain stage.

The whole process of struggle between anti- pathogenic qi and pathogenic factors, yin–yang imbalance and progression, manifesting as specific symptoms and patterns. In a narrow sense, a disease has its specific name.
The process of an overall analysis of clinical data to determine the location, etiological factors and nature of a disease at a certain stage.
The process of differentiating a disease from its whole process and its characteristics according to the etiology, underlying pathology, progression and prognosis.

The whole process of applying theories, principles, prescriptions and medicines to clinical treatment. Pattern differentiation aims to analyse the signs and symptoms collected by the four examination methods according to the fundamental theories of the eight principles, zang–fu organs, etiology and pathogenesis. Treatment refers to specific therapeutic methods directed at the differentiated pattern.

term_en: Combination of the four diagnostic methods
definition: The process of an overall analysis of clinical data collected through the four diagnostic methods and providing a diagnosis and potential treatment options.
Integrated differentiation of both pattern and disease. This helps to analyse the disease onset and development, and thus provide reliable evidence for practical treatment strategies.

term_en: Judging the inside from observing the outside
definition: A method to understand internal pathological changes through observing the external manifestations.
A method to understand patients’health condition by observing changes in their body, localized body parts, and excreta.

Bright eyes with flexible eyeballs, clear consciousness, natural facial expressions, a moist lustrous face, a fit body, smooth body movements, and even breathing. The presence of spirit indicates abundant essential qi or a mild medical condition.

Dull eyes with sluggish eyeballs, poor spirit, slow response, a complexion lacking lustre, flabby muscle and slow body movements. The insufficiency of spirit indicates insufficiency of healthy qi or mild impairment to essential qi of zang–fu organs.

Dull eyes with sluggish eyeballs, listlessness or unconsciousness, apathetic expression, slow response, a grey/dark complexion lacking lustre, weight loss and difficult body movements. The loss of spirit indicates severe damage to healthy qi and essential qi failure of zang–fu organs.

synonyms_en: The last radiance of the setting sun/the last flicker of life in a dying person
definition: Sudden‘better’signs and symptoms in patients with chronic critical conditions: a sudden change from dull eyes with sluggish eyeballs to floating brightness in the eyes; a sudden change from mental unconsciousness or listlessness to clear consciousness and mental restlessness; a sudden change from reluctance to talk and low weak voice into a talkative, clear voice; a sudden change from a grey/dark complexion to flushed cheeks; and a sudden change from no appetite and low food intake into increased appetite and hunger. The false spirit indicates collapse of healthy qi, extreme essential qi failure of zang–fu organs or imminent separation between yin and yang. This is seen as an omen for a dying person.

The actions of picking or grasping at imaginary objects, as well as the patient’s own clothes or bed linens. Often seen in delirious or semiconscious states, it can be a grave symptom in cases of extreme qi deficiency or approaching qi exhaustion.
A diagnostic method to observe colour changes of the skin, especially to the face.

With abundant qi and blood as well as functioning of zang–fu organs, a normal facial colour is moist, lustrous and non-exposed red. 2 Terminologies on diagnosis, patterns and constitution 二、诊断、病证和体质术语
The colour one was born with. It remains throughout life. It is determined by race and prenatal factors.
The colour one takes on when physiological, seasonal, climactic, geographic, diet and emotions change the colouring.
Abnormal changes in both colour and lustre of the face under a morbid state.

An abnormal but lustrous complexion, indicating that essential qi of zang–fu organs remain sufficient and stomach qi can ascend to the face. It is often seen in acute, mild conditions or yang pattern that can be easily treated and have a favourable prognosis.
